articles.text:
Business & Markets
Mercor Hits $20B Valuation After $750M Series D to Train and Test AI Agents
By James Dargan · 11 November 2026 · 1 min read
AI training startup Mercor has secured $750 million in a Series D funding round that values the company at $20 billion, the firm said on Tuesday. Benchmark, Felicis, Fundomo, Nvidia and funds managed by affiliates of Apollo were among the participants.
The San Francisco-based company started out as an AI-powered hiring platform but now connects technology companies with subject-matter experts whose knowledge is used to train, test and improve AI models and agents. Mercor said the new capital will go towards training and testing AI agents on professional tasks.
Co-CEO Brendan Foody said every job in the economy will require its own AI agents, and every company will need a way to train and evaluate those agents on its own work.
The latest valuation roughly doubles the approximately $10 billion figure Mercor reached after raising $350 million in October last year. The company counts Jack Dorsey and venture capitalist Peter Thiel among its backers.
The deal reflects strong investor appetite for AI, which has driven a sharp rise in private funding this year and produced a growing group of heavily capitalised startups with multibillion-dollar valuations. According to Crunchbase, AI-driven startups raised $102 billion in the third quarter of 2026, accounting for 64% of global venture capital.

articles.text:

OpenAI Secures $15B Funding at $1.25T Valuation
OpenAI has raised $15 billion in new capital, pushing its valuation to $1.25 trillion as the company faces intensifying competition from rival Anthropic.
Elena Whitmore
·
14 November 2026 05:15
·
2 min read
·
3,238 reads
Google'a Ekle
Capital Influx Amid Scaling Demands
OpenAI has successfully secured $15 billion in fresh funding, bringing the artificial intelligence leader to a $1.25 trillion valuation. This capital injection arrives as the company accelerates its massive infrastructure build-out, which requires significant spending on data centers and high-performance computing hardware. Recent reports indicate that Nvidia has contributed approximately $30 billion to OpenAI , while SoftBank has provided roughly $65 billion.
Financial Metrics and Market Context
The latest financing round represents half of the $30 billion target OpenAI originally sought. The valuation reflects a 47% increase over the $852 billion post-money valuation recorded in March 2026. Despite a 50% revenue growth between the second and third quarters, the firm remains heavily reliant on external capital to sustain its operations.
Anthropic is preparing for a public market debut on the Nasdaq as early as November 19.
Anthropic valuation in the upcoming IPO is expected to range between $1.2 trillion and $1.3 trillion.
Private placement commitments from investors including Google , Microsoft , and AMD total $26 billion for the Anthropic listing.
The proximity of these two major funding events highlights the extreme capital intensity of the generative AI sector. Investors are now closely watching the public markets to determine if Anthropic will command a premium over the valuations currently seen in private funding rounds.
Timing is critical. The market is shifting. Investors are demanding clearer paths to profitability as development costs mount. For OpenAI and its peers, the race for infrastructure dominance continues unabated.

articles.title: Hugging Face CEO vows to keep fighting for open source AI after Jensen Huang’s exit
articles.snippet: Hugging Face's CEO pledged to keep fighting for open source AI after Huang's exit, raising questions about Nvidia's $12.9 billion acquisition.
articles.text:
Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue briefly commented on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday, calling it a “really sad day.” Nvidia had announced its plan to acquire the platform for open source AI models in September for $12.9 billion, making it the second-largest acquisition in the company’s history, just behind that of chipmaker Groq’s assets for $20 billion in December 2025.
“This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!,” Delangue wrote on X.
This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day!
But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go! — clem 🤗 (@ClementDelangue) November 12, 2026
The post is interesting as it implies that Huang’s departure is potentially worrying to open source advocates, and he’s attempting to offer reassurance.
As Nvidia’s CEO, Huang was known as a strong advocate for open source AI and open-weight models, which is why there could be concerns about how a company that’s no longer under his leadership will now approach this space.
After Nvidia announced its plans to acquire Hugging Face, the U.S. Department of Justice began making inquiries about how the deal would impact competition in the AI market, Reuters reported in October . While Nvidia pledged that the platform would preserve open support, it would also allow the company to control a major distribution channel for AI models.
The Hugging Face deal is still scheduled to close in the first half of 2027. Requests for further comment on the deal status and whether Hugging Face has spoken yet with Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress were not returned.
Huang’s advocacy for open source and open-weight AI has long extended beyond Hugging Face. In July, the CEO published an AI policy letter as his first-ever post on the social network X . The letter, which was signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, Hugging Face, IBM, Palantir, and others, urged the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models. It said models that “anyone can download, inspect, modify, and run on their own infrastructure” are an important part of the AI ecosystem because they make AI “more accessible, adaptable, and widely available.”
Huang also wrote that open-weight models expand access to the AI economy, strengthen competition, and give customers greater control, as they know they won’t become locked into a single provider. “Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty,” his post on X stated.
For my first post, I’m sharing a letter @NVIDIA signed on why open models matter.
AI will transform every industry, power every company, and be built by every country.
Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty.… pic.twitter.com/t02bi51N4C — Jensen Huang (@JensenHuang) July 24, 2026
In August, Nvidia also announced a $6 billion deal with the coding startup Poolside to help build out an open AI ecosystem in the U.S. to help the country compete against Chinese companies like DeepSeek and Kimi K3, The Wall Street Journal reported at the time. Ferguson: $9 Billion In Third-Quarter Sales, 9.5% Growth, And Raised 2026 Guidance
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:07 AM
Ferguson: $9 Billion In Third-Quarter Sales, 9.5% Growth, And Raised 2026 Guidance
Ferguson Enterprises, a North American distributor of water and air solutions, reported third-quarter 2026 sales of $9.03 billion, representing a 9.5% increase from the prior year, supported by organic growth, acquisitions, and strong demand across non-residential markets. The company also raised its full-year sales growth outlook following continued operating momentum and the acquisition of FloWorks.
For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Ferguson generated organic sales growth of 7%, while acquisitions contributed an additional 2.7 percentage points. The company reported operating profit of $885 million, up 4.9% year over year, and adjusted operating profit of $962 million, an increase of 8.9%.
Gross margin declined 40 basis points to 30.9%, while reported operating margin decreased to 9.8% from 10.2% a year earlier. Adjusted operating margin remained unchanged at 10.7%.
Reported diluted earnings per share declined 4.9% to $3.08, compared with $3.24 in the prior-year quarter. However, adjusted diluted earnings per share increased 7.9% to $3.43, reflecting higher adjusted operating profit.
Ferguson’s U.S. business continued to drive growth, with sales increasing 10.2% year over year. Non-residential sales rose 15%, supported by large capital projects, healthy bidding activity, and demand for specialized solutions. Residential sales increased 6% despite continued weakness in new construction and repair, maintenance, and improvement activity.
The Canadian business experienced more challenging conditions, with sales declining 4.5%, reflecting divestments and unfavorable foreign exchange movements.
Acquisitions remained a central component of Ferguson’s expansion strategy. The company completed three acquisitions during the quarter, including FloWorks, Brax Company, and Rogers Supply Company. Following the quarter, Ferguson also acquired Canyon Systems, expanding its water and wastewater treatment capabilities.
Ferguson has completed 11 acquisitions during 2026, representing approximately $1.5 billion in aggregate annualized revenue. The company invested $1.7 billion in acquisitions during the third quarter, including FloWorks, while deploying $108 million in capital expenditures.
Following the FloWorks acquisition, Ferguson reported net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 1.7 times, compared with 1.0 times a year earlier.
For the first nine months of 2026, Ferguson generated $25.25 billion in sales, an increase of 6%, while adjusted operating profit increased 6.5% to $2.54 billion. Adjusted EBITDA reached $2.73 billion, up 6.9%.
Based on its year-to-date performance and the contribution from FloWorks, Ferguson increased its calendar 2026 sales growth guidance from mid-single-digit growth to approximately 7%. The company also raised the lower end of its adjusted operating margin outlook, establishing a revised range of 9.6% to 9.8%, compared with the previous range of 9.5% to 9.8%.
The updated outlook includes approximately $235 million in interest expense and $425 million in capital expenditures.
Ferguson also declared a quarterly dividend of $0.89 per share, payable January 8, 2027, to shareholders of record as of November 20, 2026.

articles.title: SolaREIT Supports Over $8.5 Billion In Clean Energy Project Value
articles.snippet:
SolaREIT has surpassed $8.5 billion in project value supported through its real estate financing, covering approximately 4.6 gigawatts of solar and battery storage capacity.
The post SolaREIT Supports Over $8.5 Billion In Clean Energy Project Value appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
SolaREIT Supports Over $8.5 Billion In Clean Energy Project Value
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:56 PM
SolaREIT Supports Over $8.5 Billion In Clean Energy Project Value
SolaREIT has surpassed $8.5 billion in project value supported through its real estate financing, covering approximately 4.6 gigawatts of solar and battery storage capacity.
The milestone represents more than $3.5 billion in additional project value since November 2025. It measures the value of associated energy projects rather than the amount of financing directly provided by SolaREIT.
The Virginia-based company offers land purchases, lease purchases and land loans across all 50 states.
Its services cover utility-scale and distributed solar, battery energy storage and related infrastructure, including substation and transmission land.
The model allows developers and project owners to access capital tied to project real estate. Management said that flexibility is important when financing conditions, procurement plans and interconnection schedules change.
Co-Founder and CEO Laura Pagliarulo described land as an asset developers can use to raise capital in a constrained funding environment.
Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operating Officer Laura Klein said transactions can close within 30 to 45 days of signing, using diligence built around information developers already hold about their projects.
Founded in 2020 as a real estate investment trust, SolaREIT is a woman-owned and led business established by clean energy industry executives.
Its team brings experience across project development, finance, real estate and community solar. The company works with both developers and landowners.
The milestone reflects growth in real estate financing as one component of renewable energy project funding.
SolaREIT’s offering focuses specifically on land, providing developers with an additional source of capital alongside the other financing needed to build and operate solar, storage and associated infrastructure.
The company said its team’s industry experience helps it evaluate complex transactions and structure financing around project timelines.
KEY QUOTES:
“We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to developers and project owners, helping them create additional value in a capital-constrained environment. It’s been another turbulent year, with higher interest rates and shifting policy, and the land under their projects is one of the few assets developers can turn into capital quickly. Surpassing $8.5 billion in project value financed reflects the trust our partners place in us. Our team has over 300 years of collective experience in the clean energy space, which allows us to help developers finance even their most complex deals.”
Laura Pagliarulo, Co-Founder And CEO Of SolaREIT
“In this market, speed and flexibility matter. With interconnection deadlines and procurement plans constantly shifting, developers need capital solutions that work on their timeline. We build our diligence on what developers already know about their projects, so we can close in 30 to 45 days from signing, providing developers with capital on a schedule they can plan around.”
Laura Klein, Chief Financial Officer And Chief Operating Officer Of SolaREIT
